tagline: Sync PRs and issues with Linear tickets automatically
metaTitle: Linear GitHub Integration: Auto Status Updates on PR Merge
metaDescription: Stop moving Linear issues by hand after every merge. GAIA updates issue status as pull requests open and merge, and tracks PR cycle time. See the setup steps.
intro:
Linear's own GitHub integration links pull requests, branches and commits to issues and moves issue status for you, with no extra tool. Connect it under Settings > Integrations > GitHub, then put the issue ID (like ENG-123) in the branch name, PR title or PR description; copying the git branch name from an issue does this for you. In each team's workflow settings, choose the status an issue moves to when you copy its branch name or open a draft PR, when a PR opens or review is requested, and when the PR merges (usually Done). You can add rules per target branch, for example In QA on merge to staging and Done on merge to main. A closing word such as "Fixes ENG-123" in the PR description also closes the issue on merge.

If that covers your team, you do not need GAIA for status updates. GAIA is for the work the native integration does not do: steps that cross more tools or need judgment. Its triggers fire on pull request events, new issues and pushed commits in the repositories you pick, and when a tracker issue is created or updated or a comment is added in a team you pick. A workflow written in plain English then acts with GAIA's tools for repositories, issues, Slack and Gmail: post a Slack summary of what merged today, draft release notes from the issues closed this week, or turn alert emails into triaged Linear issues.

An example workflow: "When a pull request is merged in acme/api, find the issue IDs in its branch name and title, comment on each issue with the PR link, and post a one-line summary to #releases in Slack."

useCases.title: Auto-update Linear issue status from PR events
useCases.description: When a PR is opened referencing an issue, GAIA moves the issue to 'In Review'. When the PR merges, GAIA marks the issue as 'Done'. The board always reflects actual code state.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from GitHub issues
useCases.description: Bug reports and feature requests filed in GitHub can automatically create corresponding tickets, ensuring the engineering backlog and the repository's issue list stay in sync.

useCases.title: PR cycle time reporting
useCases.description: GAIA tracks the time from issue creation to PR merge and generates weekly reports showing cycle time by team member and issue type to identify bottlenecks.

useCases.title: Branch naming convention checks
useCases.description: On a schedule you set, GAIA lists open pull requests in the repositories you choose and flags any whose branch name or title has no Linear issue ID, so untracked work shows up before review.

useCases.title: Release notes generation
useCases.description: When PRs are merged to main, GAIA compiles the linked issues into structured release notes organized by feature area, ready for the changelog or product announcement.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your organization and workspace. Select which repositories and teams to synchronize.

howItWorks.step: Describe the workflow in plain English
howItWorks.description: Pick a GitHub trigger (pull request event, new issue or pushed commit) or a trigger on the other tool (issue created, issue updated or comment added), then write what GAIA should do, for example "when a PR against main references a Linear issue, comment the PR link on the issue". GAIA runs each step with the matching tools.
Every workflow run is recorded, and GAIA can notify you when it acts. You can also ask GAIA at any time to compare open PRs with issue states and list the mismatches.

faqs.question: How does GAIA link a PR to an issue?
faqs.answer: GAIA looks for issue IDs in PR titles and branch names (like 'ENG-123' or 'feature/ENG-123-user-auth'). It can also parse PR descriptions for issue URLs. Most engineering teams already use these conventions.

faqs.question: What happens if a PR references multiple issues?
faqs.answer: GAIA updates all referenced issues when the PR status changes. This is common for large PRs that resolve several related issues simultaneously.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync issue fields to PR labels?
faqs.answer: Not as a live mirror. A workflow on GAIA's issue-updated trigger can add or change labels on the linked PR when an issue changes, using GAIA's repository tools. It runs once per event in one direction, so treat it as automation, not two-way sync.

faqs.question: How do I make Linear mark an issue Done when the GitHub PR merges?
faqs.answer: Use the native integration; GAIA is not needed for this. Connect the code host under Settings > Integrations, open your team's workflow settings and set the PR merge automation to Done. Put the issue ID in the branch name, PR title or description so the PR can be linked to the issue.

faqs.question: Can ticket status change on release instead of on merge?
faqs.answer: The native integration's branch rules let you set a different status per target branch, so a merge to staging can move issues to In QA and a merge to your release or main branch can move them to Done. If a release is a tag or a deploy rather than a merge, GAIA can run a workflow on pushed commits or on a schedule, find the issues that shipped and update them.

faqs.question: How do I get monitoring alerts filed as issues automatically?
faqs.answer: Start with your monitoring tool's native integrations: error trackers such as Sentry can create issues in either tracker from alerts. If your alerts arrive by email, GAIA's Gmail trigger can start a workflow on each alert email that checks for an existing open issue and, if there is none, creates one in whichever tracker you use, with the error, service and link.
